intended_object: The canonical bijection between dependent functions into a fibrewise product, ∏ᵢ (βᵢ × γᵢ), and pairs of dependent functions, (∏ᵢ βᵢ) × (∏ᵢ γᵢ). This is the universal property of the product applied pointwise. Inferred from the name, docstring and body.
explanation:
The forward map sends f to (fun i => (f i).1, fun i => (f i).2), and the inverse sends (g, h) to fun i => (g i, h i). The two maps are inverse to each other by eta for products and for functions, which the default `left_inv`/`right_inv` proofs handle. So this is exactly the standard equivalence ∏ᵢ (βᵢ × γᵢ) ≃ (∏ᵢ βᵢ) × (∏ᵢ γᵢ).

It is stated in full dependent generality. The index type is an arbitrary `Type*` and the fibre families are arbitrary. `×` needs `Type`-valued fibres; `PProd` would be the `Sort` version, but `Type*` is the conventional generality here.

The only flaw is a typo in the docstring: it says "`α → β` and `β → γ`" where it should say "`α → γ`". This does not affect the mathematics.

Mathlib has no other general declaration of this equivalence. `MeasurableEquiv.arrowProdEquivProdArrow` is a measurable-equivalence enhancement of this one, not a separate general version.
